title: Heart transplantation: indications, bicaval technique, physiology and surveillance
subject: ss-ctvs
refs: Sabiston Textbook of Surgery 22e Ch 114 (Heart Transplantation)
ISHLT Guidelines for the Care of Heart Transplant Recipients

steps.say: Heart transplantation remains the definitive option for advanced end-stage cardiac failure. Candidates present with refractory functional limitation in NYHA class IV despite maximal medical therapy. Objective cardiopulmonary exercise testing demonstrating a peak VO2 below 12 to 14 millilitres per kilogram per minute confirms listing eligibility.
steps.tx: The primary indication for **orthotopic heart transplantation** is refractory end-stage heart failure in **NYHA class IV** despite guideline-directed therapy. Objective assessment relies on cardiopulmonary exercise testing, where a **peak VO2** below 12 to 14 mL/kg/min confirms severely compromised cardiac reserve warranting listing.

steps.say: Elevated pulmonary vascular resistance is a critical gatekeeper for candidate suitability. When fixed vascular resistance exceeds 4 to 5 Wood units despite vasodilator infusions, donor right ventricular failure is inevitable. Such fixed resistance contraindicates isolated cardiac transplantation, necessitating heart-lung or ventricular assist alternatives.
steps.tx: Fixed pulmonary hypertension with **pulmonary vascular resistance** above 4 to 5 **Wood units** refractory to vasodilator challenge is an absolute contraindication to isolated transplantation. The normal unconditioned donor right ventricle cannot overcome high pulmonary impedance, resulting in acute, fatal donor **right ventricular failure**.

rows: > 4 to 5 Wood units refractory to vasodilators

steps.say: Donor organ preservation requires cold crystalloid cardioplegic arrest and topical hypothermia. Every effort must be made to restrict the cold ischemic time to under 4 to 6 hours. Prolonged storage past this window triggers ischemic reperfusion injury and leads to severe primary graft dysfunction.
steps.tx: Donor myocardial preservation employs hypothermic static storage flushed with cold **crystalloid cardioplegia**. Safe **cold ischemic time** is strictly limited to under 4 to 6 hours. Exceeding this duration dramatically elevates the risk of severe **primary graft dysfunction** and early perioperative mortality.

left.title: Preservation Principles
points: Topical slush hypothermia at 4 degrees Celsius
Safe ischemic window strictly under 4 to 6 hours

right.title: Ischemic Consequences
points: Primary graft dysfunction and low output
Severe myocardial edema and microvascular injury

steps.say: Modern surgery employs the bicaval technique instead of the older biatrial method. The surgeon constructs separate end-to-end anastomoses for the superior vena cava and inferior vena cava. This preserves intact right atrial geometry and maintains physiological tricuspid valve function.
steps.tx: The contemporary **bicaval technique** preserves anatomical **right atrial geometry** during **orthotopic transplantation**. Separate end-to-end anastomoses are fashioned for the donor left atrial cuff, inferior vena cava, superior vena cava, pulmonary artery, and ascending aorta, providing optimal hemodynamics and stable valve competence.

nodes.label: Excise recipient heart at atrial cuffs and great vessels
Suture left atrial anastomosis to pulmonary venous cuff
Perform inferior vena cava end-to-end anastomosis
Complete superior vena cava, pulmonary artery, and aortic joins

steps.say: The classical Lower-Shumway biatrial technique joined the donor heart across large atrial cuffs. Unfortunately, that created distorted atrial walls, tricuspid regurgitation, and frequent sinus node injury. The bicaval modification markedly reduces these rhythm and valve complications.
steps.tx: Compared with the historical **biatrial technique** of Lower and Shumway, the bicaval method significantly reduces postoperative **tricuspid regurgitation** and **sinus node dysfunction**. Preserving intact cavae avoids high right atrial pressures and substantially decreases the requirement for permanent pacemaker implantation across long-term follow-up.

left.title: Bicaval Technique Advantages
points: Protects sinoatrial node and sinus rhythm

right.title: Biatrial Technique Drawbacks
points: Distorts atrial geometry and annular shape

steps.say: Complete surgical transection of nerve pathways leaves the allograft completely denervated. The denervated heart loses parasympathetic vagal tone, producing a baseline resting heart rate between 90 and 110 beats per minute. Vagolytic drugs like atropine fail to produce any chronotropic response.
steps.tx: Extrinsic autonomic division results in complete **autonomic denervation** of the donor allograft. The absence of vagal tone elevates baseline **resting heart rate** to 90 to 110 beats per minute. The heart exhibits **atropine insensitivity** and carotid sinus massage elicits zero reflex slowing.

rows: Slow heart rate ramp-up and prolonged recovery

steps.say: Protocolized surveillance biopsies detect acute cellular rejection before pump failure develops. The biopsy bioptome passes down the internal jugular vein across the tricuspid valve into the right ventricular septum. Pathologists evaluate the specimen using the standardized ISHLT histologic grading system.
steps.tx: Routine surveillance for **cellular rejection** employs protocol **endomyocardial biopsy** targeting the right ventricular septum via right internal jugular access. Specimens are graded by the **ISHLT grading** system (grade 0R to 3R) to identify myocyte necrosis and guide pulse corticosteroid therapy.

nodes.label: Percutaneous right internal jugular sheath insertion
Advance bioptome across tricuspid valve under fluoroscopy
Sample 4-6 pieces of right ventricular endomyocardium

steps.say: Cardiac allograft vasculopathy remains the leading cause of late graft failure and death. Accelerated intimal proliferation causes diffuse, concentric narrowing throughout the coronary arterial tree. Because the denervated heart feels no chest pain, annual coronary surveillance by angiography or intravascular ultrasound is essential beyond one year.
steps.tx: **Cardiac allograft vasculopathy** represents the primary determinant of **late graft failure** and mortality after heart transplantation, characterized by diffuse **concentric intimal hyperplasia** across epicardial coronary vessels. Because denervation causes silent ischemia, regular coronary angiography beyond 1 year is mandatory to detect disease.
